title: Audio crashes on Linux - "couldn't open play stream: Device or resource busy"
author: celerizer
body:
### Describe the feature or issue.

Some known working games are crashing for me when compiling touchHLE on Linux, whereas they work on Windows or while using the Windows build under Proton.

Affected games on my end are Earthworm Jim and Rayman 2, where they retrieve a null audio device. Meanwhile, Resident Evil 4 and Crash Nitro Kart 3D work perfectly with audio.

OS: Debian GNU/Linux 13 (trixie) x86_64
Kernel: Linux 6.12.48+deb13-amd64
DE: KDE Plasma 6.3.6
WM: KWin (X11)

comments.author: celerizer
comments.body: After some more testing, it seems these games actually do work, but only the first time between resets. Maybe `alcCloseDevice` needs to be done somewhere when touchHLE exits if the game doesn't.

comments.author: hikari-no-yume
comments.body: That's… very strange. If the OS isn't cleaning up handles properly when a process exists, I would consider that an OS bug.

comments.author: celerizer
comments.body: I'm going to close this and just say it was my own error; not having up-to-date pipewire or pulseaudio dev packages made it try to grab my audio device exclusively which caused problems

comments.author: hikari-no-yume
comments.body: Ahh. I did wonder if it could be some weird device exclusivity issue, because in some games, it could be the case that touchHLE opens multiple handles to the same audio device (if that's how OpenAL-Soft works — I don't know!). Thanks for the info.
